production.note: US model years 2014-2015. Start: GM Authority's 2014 Camaro Z/28 page, reproducing GM's specifications, covers the 2014 model year, which "began arriving in dealerships across the United States in the spring of 2014" (source gmauthority-2014-camaro-z28). Chevrolet's 2015 brochure lists the Z/28. End: Chevrolet's 2016 brochure describes the all-new sixth-generation car and lists only the 1LT, 2LT, 1SS and 2SS; no Z/28 (source chevrolet-camaro-brochure-2016).

body.note: Coupe only. GM's 2014 table: "Four-passenger, front-engine, rear-drive coupe" (source gmauthority-2014-camaro-z28).

configuration.note: "7.0L LS7 V8, aluminum block and heads"

displacementL.note: 7,008 cc. GM's 2014 specification table as printed by GM Authority: "Displacement (cu in / cc): 427 / 7008". Chevrolet's 2015 brochure gives "7.0L" (source chevrolet-camaro-brochure-2015).

aspiration.note: Inferred: the brochure lists the ZL1's engine as "supercharged" and the Z/28's LS7 without forced induction.

transmission.note: Manual only. Brochure: "TREMEC TR6060 6-speed manual transmission with close-ratio gearset". GM's 2014 table: "Transmission: Tremec TR6060 six-speed manual" (source gmauthority-2014-camaro-z28).

powerHp.note: Quote (Chevrolet 2015 brochure, Z/28 column): "7.0L LS7 V8, aluminum block and heads" ... "505 @ 6100 rpm". GM's 2014 specification table as printed by GM Authority: "Horsepower (hp / kW @ rpm): 505 / 376 @ 6100 (SAE certified)" (source gmauthority-2014-camaro-z28), so the rating was the same for both model years.

weightLb.note: Manufacturer curb weight, 2015 model year (the Z/28 came only as a manual coupe). Quote (Chevrolet 2015 brochure, curb weight row, Z/28 column): "3,820 lbs." GM's 2014 specification table as printed by GM Authority gives the same figure with a qualifier: "Curb weight (lb / kg): 3820 / 1732 (without air conditioning)" (source gmauthority-2014-camaro-z28); GM Authority says air conditioning was a $1,150 option in 2014, so the figure describes the standard car. The 2014 Chevrolet brochure could not be opened (auto-brochures.com returned HTTP 429 every time), so the reference year is 2015, the earliest year with an opened Chevrolet-hosted figure. SlashGear's October 2013 first-ride article prints "3,836 pounds" (source slashgear-z28-2013); see discrepancies.

discrepancies.reason: Pre-production figure: SlashGear (Vincent Nguyen, 16 October 2013) wrote "3,836 pounds" from a pre-launch ride event, months before the car reached dealers; Chevrolet's 2015 brochure and GM's 2014 specification table both give 3,820 lb.
discrepancies.resolution: Used Chevrolet's 3,820 lb, which GM's own tables give for both model years.
